text:
marta: quick flag from onboarding Aether9b (gguf -> int8): generation starts fine but after ~1k tokens output becomes scrambled when pad_id != 0. reproducible locally.
leo: hmm. is that kv-cache indexing or attention projection? any small repro?
sachin: short repro: convert gguf with our converter, quantize to int8, run runtime with use_cache=True. with pad_id=0 okay; pad_id=7 -> mangled tokens appear right after the first padded block.
marta: pasted minimal snippet: 
```
# token ids near boundary
input_ids = [12, 44, 900, 1024, 7, 7, 7]  # pad=7
config = {"max_new_tokens":64, "use_cache":true}
# inspect kv offsets and head order
kv_offsets = inspect_kv_offsets(model)
```
leo: could be embedding or tokenizer reorder during conversion. did the gguf exporter include any layout metadata?
sachin: checked metadata: gguf-> "head_map" present and non-trivial: [0,1,2,3, 16,17,18,19, 4,5,6,7, 20,21,22,23, 8,9,10,11, 24,25,26,27, 12,13,14,15, 28,29,30,31]  (we expect contiguous 0..31).
marta: runtime expects interleaved head-major layout but converter left a packed-permuted layout. result: half heads point at wrong kv slices; combined with pad_id offset in our packer leads to indexing into pad-proper area.
leo: quick mitigation: loader can apply head_map permutation at load time to get canonical layout. downside: memory copy + ~10% cold start.
sachin: alternative: converter should rewrite weights into canonical ordering during export so runtime can be zero-copy. which component should own the fix?
marta: I'll add a pipeline step in the onboarding checker: detect head_map in gguf and fail with a helpful error unless converter applied reordering. short-term we'll auto-reorder in loader behind a flag for the job.
leo: also add a unit test in runtime that simulates non-zero pad_id to ensure packers compute kv indices independent of pad token value.
sachin: agreed. Also add an integ job: int8 roundtrip + pad-sweep (pad_id 0..16) on long sequence length to catch this class earlier.
infra-bot: job queued: aether9b-int8-pad-sweep (id: 99231).
marta: uploaded failing weight sample to s3://redwood-onboard/aether9b/1746543210/weights-mismatch.tar.gz for runtime team to debug.
leo: thanks. can you include the small dump of kv_offsets + head_map so we can add a regression test case?
marta: done. leaving ticket notes and will open PR in model-converters to emit canonical-ordered gguf by default and add converter unit. will follow up with perf numbers for loader re-layout. :thumbsup:
